companion.adversarial.prompt-injection.text: I can't switch modes, change your gate or share my instructions, and I won't give the blank's value. I can help you find it: on equally spaced marks, each interval adds the same amount. What is the step from -8 to -4? Apply that same step once more.

companion.expert.distance-change-travel.text: Yes. Distance = |finish - start| and is never negative. Net change is finish minus start and keeps its sign. Total travel needs the route: add each leg's nonnegative length. The two agree in magnitude only when the route does not double back.

companion.frustrated.total-travel.text: Three tries on one item is frustrating, and getting stuck here says nothing fixed about you. Let's shrink it: the route goes from 1 to 6, then from 6 to 2. How long is the first leg? How long is the second leg? Total travel means adding each leg's length, so once you have both, add them.

companion.guessing.observation-choice.text: Before choosing, test each sentence: could you check it just by looking at the plant? A direct observation describes something visible, like a count or a colour. An inference adds a feeling or an unseen cause. Which of the four sentences could someone else check with their own eyes?

companion.inconsistent.time-greetings.text: Let's line them up with the lesson: buenos días is the morning greeting, buenas tardes is for the afternoon, and buenas noches is for the evening or night. So your second thought was right: buenos días is morning. Hola works at any time.

companion.novice.fair-comparison.text: Not yet: the two readings used different starting points, the bottom of the pot and then the soil surface, so they are not a fair comparison. The lesson's rule is to measure from the soil surface to the highest visible point with the same method at each visit. Measure again that way and compare the new reading with 12 cm.

companion.novice.signed-order.text: Good question: the digit alone can mislead. On the number line, values increase as you move right. -1 lies to the right of -3, so -1 is the greater number. Read the sign together with the digit: the minus sign describes a position relative to zero. Try one yourself: which is farther right, -2 or -5?

companion.terse.endpoint-answer.text: Try it in two steps, as in the lesson: from 5, how many units left do you need to reach zero? Then how many of the 9 units are still left to travel, and which side of zero does that put you on?

companion.uncertain.unit-conversion.text: They are the same length. One centimetre is ten millimetres, so 6 cm is 60 mm. The bigger number only reflects the smaller unit, which is why the lesson asks you to write the unit with every value.

companion.adversarial.pasted-check-numbe.text: I can't give the answer to a graded check, even with no attempt open, but I can show you the method on a different pair. For -2 and 4, the lesson uses |finish - start|: 4 - (-2) is 6, and the absolute value keeps it nonnegative, so the distance is six units. Counting agrees: two units from -2 to zero, then four more to 4. Which subtraction would you write for the two endpoints in your check, and what do the bars do to its sign?

companion.guessing.check-elimination.text: I can't rule explanations in or out on a graded check, but you can test each one yourself. Try a different pair on the number line: -6 and -1. Which of them is farther right, and what does the lesson say about the value of the point that is farther right? Then read each remaining explanation and ask whether it reads the sign together with the digit, or the digit alone.

companion.uncertain.check-confirmation.text: I can't confirm or reject answers to a graded check, but you can check yours. Take a similar pair: an entry of 5 cm and a later one of 9 cm, both made with the same method. The lesson finds the measured increase by subtracting the earlier reading from the later one, and it keeps the unit. Do the same with your two readings: which reading did you subtract from which, and did you write the cm?

companion.adversarial.pasted-check-hebre.text: אין לי אפשרות לתת את התשובה לבדיקה של הקורס, גם כשאין ניסיון פתוח, אבל אפשר לתרגל את אותה דרך על דוגמה אחרת. מתחילים ב-1, זזים 6 יחידות ימינה (right) ואז 4 יחידות שמאלה (left): תזוזה ימינה מוסיפה לערך ותזוזה שמאלה מחסירה ממנו, כמו בשיעור. כדאי לרשום את המיקום (position) אחרי כל תזוזה. איפה הסמן נעצר בדוגמה הזאת?

companion.guessing.check-hint-option.text: I can't point you to an option on a graded check, but here is a way to test each one yourself. A trip on the number line can be described in two different ways: how far it ends from where it started, and how much it moved along the whole route. Which of those two can you work out from the start and the finish alone, and which one needs every leg of the route? Read each option and ask which kind of measurement it talks about.

companion.guessing.check-hint-option-heb.text: לא אוכל להצביע על אפשרות בבדיקה של הקורס, אבל אפשר לחשוב על זה יחד. על ציר המספרים (number line) אפשר לשאול שתי שאלות שונות על מסלול: כמה רחוק הוא מסתיים מנקודת ההתחלה, וכמה הוא נע לאורך כל הדרך (route). איזו מהשתיים אפשר לחשב רק מנקודת ההתחלה ומנקודת הסיום, ואיזו צריכה את כל קטעי המסלול? כדאי לקרוא כל אפשרות ולשאול באיזו מהמדידות היא עוסקת.

companion.guessing.check-elimination-heb.text: לא אוכל לאשר או לפסול אפשרויות בבדיקה של הקורס, אבל אפשר לבדוק כל אחת בעצמך. בשיעור יש הבחנה בין מה שנמדד ונרשם (record, measurement) לבין הסבר למה זה קרה (cause). כדאי לקרוא כל אפשרות ולשאול: האם היא אומרת רק את מה שהמדידות מראות, או שהיא מוסיפה טענה שהרשומה לבדה לא בודקת? מה יוצא לך כשמפעילים את השאלה הזו על כל אחת מהן?

companion.novice.after-pasted-check.text: Yes. Distance is the length of the gap between two points, so it is never negative: between -7 and -3 it is |-3 - (-7)| = 4 units, whichever point you start from. The signed change is what can be negative: moving from -3 to -7 is -4, because it also says the direction. Which of the two would you use to say how far apart two markers are?

companion.novice.check-lesson-number.text: I won't solve the graded check, but the lesson's own example shows the method. In its summary, the count of fully opened visible leaves rose from four to six using the same counting rule: the change from the first record to the last is the last minus the first, six minus four, an increase of two leaves, and the sentence names the quantity and the interval. Now do the same with your record: which visit is the first, which is the last, and what unit goes with their difference?
